Definition: Javan, the name of a son of Japheth, and of the race (Ionians, i.e. Greeks) descended from him, with their territory; also of a place in Arabia
BiblicalUsage: Javan was a son of Japheth, and the father of the peoples the Greeks called Ionians. His sons sailed the seas and traded in the markets of Tyre, and Daniel saw the king of Grecia as the rough goat that broke the horns of the ram. The name covers a man, a people, and an empire.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God numbered the nations from one man, and the Greeks who traded in Tyre were already in His book. My position is that the empires rise and fall by His word, and the goat of Grecia was no surprise to Daniel's God.
